optionExplanations.C: Correct – One of the five lenses: conformance to requirements.
optionExplanations.D: Correct – One of the five lenses: innate excellence, “I know it when I see it”.

questions.question: UPI handled about 698 million transactions/day (Dec 2025). Which computed figures are correct?

options.text: At 99.9% success, about 6.98 lakh payments fail per day
Monthly volume of 21.63 billion over 31 days gives roughly 698 million/day
At Six Sigma (3.4 DPMO), about 2,400 payments fail per day
At 99.9% success, about 69.8 lakh payments fail per day

questions.explanation: A: Correct – 698 × 10⁶ × 0.001 = 698,000 = 6.98 lakh. B: Correct – 21.63 × 10⁹/31 ≈ 697.7 × 10⁶. C: Correct – 698 × 3.4 = 2373 ≈ 2,400. D: Incorrect – Off by a factor of 10; 0.1% of 698 million is 6.98 lakh.

optionExplanations.D: Incorrect – Off by a factor of 10; 0.1% of 698 million is 6.98 lakh.

questions.hint: Revisit Quality Management slide 9. 3 of the 4 options are correct.

questions.question: Mumbai dabbawalas deliver about 130,000 lunches a day. Which statements are arithmetically correct?

options.text: At 99.9% accuracy, about 130 lunches/day would go wrong or be missed
At Six Sigma, about 0.44 errors/day are expected
At Six Sigma, about 44 errors/day are expected
At 99.9% accuracy, roughly one wrong lunch every two days is expected

questions.explanation: A: Correct – 130,000 × 0.001 = 130. B: Correct – 130,000 × 3.4 × 10⁻⁶ ≈ 0.442. C: Incorrect – Off by a factor of 100. D: Incorrect – That describes the Six Sigma case (0.44/day), not 99.9%.

optionExplanations.C: Incorrect – Off by a factor of 100.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect – That describes the Six Sigma case (0.44/day), not 99.9%.

questions.hint: Revisit Quality Management slide 9. 2 of the 4 options are correct.
